questions.q: Describe the location and size of India.
answer: India lies entirely in the Northern and Eastern hemispheres.

answer.text: Its mainland extends between latitudes 8°4′ N and 37°6′ N, and longitudes 68°7′ E and 97°25′ E. The Tropic of Cancer, at 23°30′ N, passes through the middle of the country, dividing it into roughly equal northern and southern parts.

India is the seventh largest country in the world, with an area of about 3.28 million square kilometres, which is about 2.4 per cent of the world's land area. It has a long coastline and vast land frontiers.
It shares land boundaries with Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar and Bangladesh, and has Sri Lanka and the Maldives as island neighbours to the south.

questions.q: What is India's Standard Meridian, and why is a single standard time used for the whole country?

answer.text: The Standard Meridian of India is the longitude of 82°30′ E, which passes through Mirzapur in Uttar Pradesh. The time along this meridian is taken as Indian Standard Time, which is five and a half hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.

India stretches across about thirty degrees of longitude from Gujarat in the west to Arunachal Pradesh in the east, so the sun rises about two hours earlier in the east than in the west. If each place kept its own local time, there would be great confusion. To avoid this, the time of the central 82°30′ E meridian is adopted as the single standard time for the whole country.
